sections.subtitle: Inženjer računalnih mreža koji je zamijenio kabele za stranačku logistiku
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Matija Stepanić postavlja uvodno pitanje 'Tko je Ivan Orlović?', gost se predstavlja u studiju
sections.content:
Nova epizoda podcasta **Domovina TV** otvara se pozdravom voditelja Matije Stepanića, koji u studiju ugošćuje **Ivana Orlovića**, organizacijskog tajnika stranke Most, uz napomenu da se radi i o njegovu prijatelju i kumu.

Na izravno pitanje tko je zapravo Ivan Orlović, gost se predstavlja bez uvijanja: **34 godine, suprug i otac troje djece**, po struci inženjer računalnih mreža. U struci je, kaže, radio sve do prije nekoliko mjeseci, a politički je angažiran već dulje vrijeme – **od kraja 2018. godine**, i to isključivo kroz Most.

Početkom ove godine, objašnjava, ukazana mu je "čast i prilika" da preuzme mjesto organizacijskog tajnika stranke. Prihvatio je, a misiju opisuje kratko: posložiti Most "što je bolje moguće". Naglašava pritom da je naslijedio **solidnu situaciju**, ali da po njegovu uvjerenju uvijek može bolje – u svakom poslu, pa tako i u organizacijskom ustroju političke stranke.
sections.subtitle_en: Computer network engineer who replaced cables with party logistics
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Matija Stepanić asks the introductory question 'Who is Ivan Orlović?', the guest introduces himself in the studio
sections.content_en:
The new episode of the **Domovina TV** podcast opens with a greeting from the host Matija Stepanić, who hosts **Ivan Orlović**, organizational secretary of the Most party, in the studio, with the note that he is also his friend and godfather.

To the direct question of who Ivan Orlović actually is, the guest introduces himself straightforwardly: **34 years old, husband and father of three children**, a computer network engineer by profession. In his profession, he says, he worked until a few months ago, and has been politically engaged for quite some time – **since the end of 2018**, and exclusively through Most.

At the beginning of this year, he explains, he was given the "honor and opportunity" to take over the position of organizational secretary of the party. He accepted, and describes the mission briefly: to organize Most "as best as possible". He emphasizes at the same time that he inherited a **solid situation**, but that in his conviction things can always be better – in every job, including in the organizational structure of a political party.

sections.subtitle: Što zapravo radi organizacijski tajnik: od ljudstva i financija do revizije javnog novca
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Orlović nabraja poslove organizacijskog tajnika – ljudstvo, uredi, financije, pravni akti
sections.content:
Voditelj želi znati kako izgleda tjedna operativa jednog organizacijskog tajnika. Orlović odgovara da je riječ o **statutarno vrlo bitnoj funkciji** koja ima dvostruku prirodu.

S jedne strane, to je **politička pozicija** – organizacijski tajnik je član predsjedništva stranke i time sudjeluje u kreiranju samih politika Mosta. S druge strane, tu je operativni dio koji je, kako kaže, "preširok spektar" da bi se ukratko objasnio.

Ipak, nabraja ključne odgovornosti:

- **rukovođenje kompletnim ljudstvom i zaposlenicima**
- **koordinacija rada svih ureda**, uključujući Središnji ured
- odgovornost za **financije stranke**
- odgovornost za **sve pravne akte i reviziju**
- odgovornost za **trošenje javnog novca**

Za sve navedeno, ističe, organizacijski tajnik odgovara **zajedno s predsjednikom stranke** – što jasno pokazuje da se ne radi samo o administrativnoj, nego i o vrlo izloženoj funkciji.
sections.subtitle_en: What does an organizational secretary actually do: from personnel and finances to the audit of public money
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Orlović lists the duties of the organizational secretary – personnel, offices, finances, legal acts
sections.content_en:
The host wants to know what the weekly operations of an organizational secretary look like. Orlović replies that it is a **statutarily very important function** that has a dual nature.

On one hand, it is a **political position** – the organizational secretary is a member of the party presidency and thus participates in creating the very policies of Most. On the other hand, there is the operational part which is, as he says, "too broad a spectrum" to be explained briefly.

Nevertheless, he lists the key responsibilities:

- **management of the entire personnel and employees**
- **coordination of the work of all offices**, including the Central Office
- responsibility for the **party's finances**
- responsibility for **all legal acts and audit**
- responsibility for the **spending of public money**

For all of the above, he points out, the organizational secretary is accountable **together with the party president** – which clearly shows that it is not only an administrative, but also a very exposed function.

sections.subtitle: Mreža ureda po Hrvatskoj: od Metkovića do Osijeka, a uskoro i Rijeka
sections.screenshot_description: Gost nabraja gradove u kojima Most ima urede i najavljuje otvaranje ureda u Rijeci
sections.content:
Na pitanje koliko ureda Most trenutačno ima u Hrvatskoj, Orlović nabraja postojeću mrežu:

- **Središnji ured u Zagrebu**
- **Split**
- **Osijek**
- **Zaprešić**
- **Velika Gorica**
- **Koprivnica**
- **Metković**

Stranka je, kaže, trenutačno **u procesu osnivanja organizacija u svim županijama**, s ciljem da se do kraja godine otvore uredi u svim županijama, odnosno u najvećim gradovima tih županija. Prvi sljedeći na redu je **ured u Rijeci**, koji bi trebao biti otvoren vrlo skoro.

Kad je riječ o zaposlenima, brojka je skromnija nego što bi se moglo očekivati. Uz samog Orlovića, stranka zapošljava **još sedam ljudi**:

- **dvije djevojke u PR i digital timu**
- **dva regionalna koordinatora** – jedan za zagrebačku regiju, drugi za područje Rijeke, Kvarnera, Istre i Gorskog kotara
- **zaposlenica u splitskom uredu**
- **regionalni koordinator u Metkoviću**, koji pokriva Dubrovačko-neretvansku županiju

Orlović pritom naknadno napominje da Most ured ima i u Metkoviću, što je ranije u nabrajanju gotovo preskočio.
sections.subtitle_en: Network of offices across Croatia: from Metković to Osijek, and soon Rijeka as well
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest lists the cities in which Most has offices and announces the opening of an office in Rijeka
sections.content_en:
To the question of how many offices Most currently has in Croatia, Orlović lists the existing network:

- **Central office in Zagreb**
- **Split**
- **Osijek**
- **Zaprešić**
- **Velika Gorica**
- **Koprivnica**
- **Metković**

The party is, he says, currently **in the process of establishing organizations in all counties**, with the goal of opening offices in all counties by the end of the year, that is, in the largest cities of those counties. The first next in line is the **office in Rijeka**, which should be opened very soon.

When it comes to employees, the figure is more modest than might be expected. Along with Orlović himself, the party employs **seven more people**:

- **two girls in the PR and digital team**
- **two regional coordinators** – one for the Zagreb region, the other for the area of Rijeka, Kvarner, Istra, and Gorski kotar
- **a female employee in the Split office**
- **a regional coordinator in Metković**, who covers Dubrovačko-neretvanska County

Orlović at the same time subsequently notes that Most also has an office in Metković, which he almost skipped earlier in the listing.

sections.subtitle: Oko 70.000 eura po zastupniku godišnje – kako se novcem poreznih obveznika financira politika
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava Zakon o financiranju političkih stranaka i iznose po saborskom zastupniku
sections.content:
Voditelj otvara temu koja rijetko dolazi u fokus: **kako se političke stranke uopće financiraju** kako bi mogle operativno funkcionirati, s obzirom na to da su političke stranke ustavna kategorija, a novac dolazi iz državnog proračuna.

Orlović objašnjava da postoji **Zakon o financiranju političkih stranaka**, koji definira dva odvojena kanala:

1. **Državni proračun** – iznos ovisi o **broju saborskih zastupnika** koje stranka ima u Hrvatskom saboru.
2. **Lokalna samouprava** – stranke dobivaju sredstva i s obzirom na broj **lokalnih, gradskih i županijskih vijećnika odnosno zastupnika**.

Kad je riječ o konkretnim brojkama, Orlović navodi da je prosjek **oko 70.000 eura godišnje po saborskom zastupniku**, uz napomenu da su to javno dostupni podaci i približna cifra. Voditelj to nadopunjuje podatkom da je riječ o postotku od **0,105 posto svih proračunskih prihoda u prethodnoj godini**.

Posebno zanimljiv detalj koji gost ističe jest **poticaj za veću zastupljenost žena u politici**: za žene se dobiva **dodatnih deset posto** subvencije, što je mehanizam osmišljen kako bi se žene više angažirale u političkom životu.
sections.subtitle_en: Around 70,000 euros per representative annually – how politics is financed with taxpayers' money
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the Law on the Financing of Political Parties and the amounts per parliamentary deputy
sections.content_en:
The host opens a topic that rarely comes into focus: **how political parties are financed at all** so that they can function operationally, given that political parties are a constitutional category, and the money comes from the state budget.

Orlović explains that there is the **Law on the Financing of Political Parties**, which defines two separate channels:

1. **State budget** – the amount depends on the **number of members of parliament** the party has in the Hrvatski sabor.
2. **Local self-government** – parties also receive funds based on the number of **local, city, and county councilors, respectively representatives**.

When it comes to concrete figures, Orlović states that the average is **around 70,000 euros per year per member of parliament**, with the note that these are publicly available data and an approximate figure. The host supplements this with the information that it is a percentage of **0.105 percent of all budget revenues in the previous year**.

A particularly interesting detail that the guest highlights is the **incentive for greater representation of women in politics**: for women, an **additional ten percent** of subsidy is received, which is a mechanism designed so that women would become more engaged in political life.
keywords_en: Law on the Financing of Political Parties

sections.subtitle: Sedam zastupnika plus jedan: kako je Josip Jurčević završio u klubu Mosta
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Orlović objašnjava status nezavisnog zastupnika Josipa Jurčevića unutar kluba Mosta
sections.content:
Na pitanje o brojnosti kluba, Orlović pojašnjava da Most trenutačno ima **sedam zastupnika**, a klub broji **ukupno osam** jer mu se priključio i nezavisni zastupnik **profesor Josip Jurčević**.

Administrativno gledano, ističe, situacija je specifična. Financiranje se, naime, **gleda prema listi s parlamentarnih izbora 2024. godine**, a Jurčević nije bio na listi Mosta – ušao je u Sabor na **listi Domovinskog pokreta**. Zbog toga, kaže Orlović, "administrativno nema veze s nama".

Gost podsjeća na politički slijed događaja: nakon što je Domovinski pokret podržao HDZ, Jurčević nije bio dio te odluke, potom je izašao iz njihova kluba, a u dogledno se vrijeme priključio klubu Mosta.

Suradnju s njim Orlović opisuje kao **fenomenalnu**, a samog Jurčevića kao čovjeka koji je "ne samo politička nego životna enciklopedija, povijesna enciklopedija". Naglašava da se od njega može puno naučiti, i to ne samo o povijesti Republike Hrvatske, nego i o **ukupnoj povijesti Hrvata još od davnina**.
sections.subtitle_en: Seven representatives plus one: how Josip Jurčević ended up in the Most club
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Orlović explains the status of independent representative Josip Jurčević within the Most club
sections.content_en:
To the question about the size of the club, Orlović clarifies that Most currently has **seven representatives**, and the club numbers **a total of eight** because the independent representative **Professor Josip Jurčević** also joined it.

Administratively speaking, he points out, the situation is specific. Financing is, namely, **looked at according to the list from the 2024 parliamentary elections**, and Jurčević was not on the list of Most – he entered the Sabor on the **list of Domovinski pokret**. Because of that, says Orlović, "administratively has nothing to do with us".

The guest recalls the political sequence of events: after Domovinski pokret supported HDZ, Jurčević was not part of that decision, then he left their club, and in due time joined the club of Most.

Orlović describes the cooperation with him as **phenomenal**, and Jurčević himself as a man who is "not only a political but a life encyclopedia, a historical encyclopedia". He emphasizes that a lot can be learned from him, and that not only about the history of the Republic of Croatia, but also about the **overall history of Croats since ancient times**.

sections.subtitle: Bez ijednog potpisa: 14 nekažnjavanih ljudi dovoljno je za izlazak na parlamentarne izbore
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava da za parlamentarne izbore nisu potrebni potpisi podrške, samo potvrde o nekažnjavanju
sections.content:
Voditelja zanima što bi trebao učiniti običan građanin koji bi želio sastaviti vlastitu nezavisnu listu za parlamentarne izbore **2028. ili 2032. godine** – koliko potpisa treba prikupiti i kako uopće funkcionira taj dio sustava.

Odgovor je za mnoge iznenađujući: **za izbore za Sabor potpisi uopće ne postoje.**

Orlović pojašnjava mehaniku:

- netko može **osnovati stranku** i izaći, primjerice, u tri izborne jedinice
- ključno je da ima **14 ljudi koji nisu kažnjavani** i koji su spremni stati na listu
- **nije potrebna pokrivenost u svih deset izbornih jedinica** – moguće je izaći samo u Zagrebu, u tri izborne jedinice, ili u dvije s 28 ljudi
- jedini je uvjet **potvrda o nekažnjavanju**

Voditelj sažima taj podatak gotovo nevjerojatnom konstatacijom: praktički **bilo kojih četrnaest ljudi u Hrvatskoj koji se skupe mogu imati svoju izbornu listu**. Orlović potvrđuje, uz ogradu da je četrnaest ljudi dovoljno za jednu izbornu jedinicu, te dodaje još jedan bitan detalj – **kandidat ne mora biti u izbornoj jedinici u kojoj je prijavljen**.

Listu je, doznaje se kasnije u razgovoru, potrebno samo predati **Državnom izbornom povjerenstvu**, bez ijednog potpisa podrške.
sections.subtitle_en: Without a single signature: 14 unconvicted people are enough to run in parliamentary elections
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that for parliamentary elections signatures of support are not required, only certificates of no criminal record
sections.content_en:
The host is interested in what an ordinary citizen who would like to compile their own independent list for the parliamentary elections in **2028 or 2032** should do – how many signatures need to be collected and how that part of the system works at all.

The answer is surprising to many: **for the Sabor elections, signatures do not exist at all.**

Orlović clarifies the mechanics:

- someone can **found a party** and run, for example, in three constituencies
- the key is to have **14 people who have not been convicted** and who are ready to stand on the list
- **coverage in all ten constituencies is not required** – it is possible to run only in Zagreb, in three constituencies, or in two with 28 people
- the only condition is a **certificate of no criminal record**

The host summarizes this fact with an almost unbelievable statement: practically **any fourteen people in Croatia who gather together can have their own electoral list**. Orlović confirms, with the caveat that fourteen people are enough for one constituency, and adds another important detail – **the candidate does not have to be in the constituency in which they are registered**.

The list, it is revealed later in the conversation, only needs to be submitted to the **State Election Commission**, without a single signature of support.

sections.subtitle: Zagrepčanin koji brani Liku: slučaj Zvonimira Troskota i pitanje 'uvezenih' kandidata
sections.screenshot_description: Gost navodi primjer Zvonimira Troskota kao kandidata u sedmoj izbornoj jedinici
sections.content:
Voditelj pita što gost misli o mogućnosti da netko bude kandidat u izbornoj jedinici u kojoj nema ni prebivalište ni boravište – koje su prednosti, a koji nedostaci takvog rješenja.

Orlović odgovara konkretnim primjerom iz vlastite stranke: **Zvonimir Troskot** je Zagrepčanin, ali već godinama **terenski djeluje u sedmoj izbornoj jedinici**. Nabraja njegove aktivnosti:

- javno je progovarao o **Kosinjskom polju**, gdje se planiralo iseliti ljude i napraviti akumulacijsko jezero, čemu su se mještani protivili
- bavio se lokalnim temama i problemima tog područja kroz terenske aktivnosti
- nedavno je, kako se pojavilo i u medijima, **otkrio otrovni otpad u Lici**

Zaključak gosta je jasan: budući da se netko već godinama bavi problemima ljudi iz određene izborne jedinice, **prirodno je da ondje i bude kandidat**, bez obzira na to odakle formalno dolazi. "Ne mislim da je to loše samo po sebi", kaže Orlović.

Ono što po njegovu mišljenju **jest loše** jest sasvim drugi problem – **prevelik broj neuravnoteženih izbornih jedinica**, iako su, priznaje, sada donekle popravljene u odnosu na ranije stanje.
sections.subtitle_en: A Zagreb native who defends Lika: the case of Zvonimir Troskot and the question of 'imported' candidates
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest cites the example of Zvonimir Troskot as a candidate in the seventh electoral district
sections.content_en:
The host asks what the guest thinks about the possibility of someone being a candidate in a constituency in which they have neither permanent nor temporary residence – what are the advantages, and what are the disadvantages of such a solution.

Orlović responds with a concrete example from his own party: **Zvonimir Troskot** is a Zagreb native, but for years he has been **active in the field in the seventh constituency**. He lists his activities:

- he spoke out publicly about **Kosinjsko polje**, where there were plans to displace people and create a reservoir, which the locals opposed
- he dealt with local topics and problems of that area through field activities
- recently, as also reported in the media, he **uncovered toxic waste in Lika**

The guest's conclusion is clear: since someone has already been dealing for years with the problems of the people from a certain constituency, **it is natural for them to be a candidate there**, regardless of where they formally come from. "I do not think that is bad in itself," says Orlović.

What in his opinion **is bad** is an entirely different problem – **an excessive number of unbalanced constituencies**, although, he admits, they are now somewhat improved compared to the earlier state.

sections.subtitle: Jedna izborna jedinica, tri posto praga i dva preferencijalna glasa – recept za demokratičniju Hrvatsku
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Orlović iznosi svoj prijedlog izborne reforme: jedna izborna jedinica i prag od 3 posto
sections.content:
Orlović iznosi svoj osobni stav o tome kako bi izborni sustav trebao izgledati. Najbolje bi, tvrdi, bilo da je **cijela država jedna izborna jedinica**, odnosno da granica uopće nema.

Uz to predlaže još dvije izmjene:

- **više preferencijalnih glasova** – da se uz jedan preferencijalni glas može birati barem još jedan, ako ne i dva
- **spuštanje izbornog praga s pet na tri posto**

To su, kaže, mjesta na kojima se hrvatska parlamentarna demokracija još može bitno unaprijediti.

Sam **parlamentarni sustav** pritom brani kao dobar model. Smatra ga **boljim od predsjedničkog i polupredsjedničkog**, jer u tim sustavima jedna osoba u pravilu postaje "šef". Kao primjer navodi **Francusku i Emmanuela Macrona** te **Ameriku i Donalda Trumpa** – riječ je o ljudima koji svojim imenom, prezimenom i karakterom određuju vrlo mnogo.

Priznaje da je i u Hrvatskoj **premijer broj jedan izvršne vlasti**, ali ključna je razlika u tome što on iza sebe ipak mora imati **većinu od 76 ruku**, što Orlović smatra demokratičnijim od modela u kojem odlučuje jedna osoba.
sections.subtitle_en: One constituency, a three percent threshold, and two preferential votes – a recipe for a more democratic Croatia
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Orlović presents his proposal for electoral reform: one electoral unit and a 3 percent threshold
sections.content_en:
Orlović presents his personal stance on how the electoral system should look. It would be best, he claims, if **the entire country were one electoral district**, that is, if there were no borders at all.

In addition, he proposes two more changes:

- **more preferential votes** – that along with one preferential vote, at least one more, if not two, can be chosen
- **lowering the electoral threshold from five to three percent**

These are, he says, areas where Croatian parliamentary democracy can still be significantly improved.

At the same time, he defends the **parliamentary system** itself as a good model. He considers it **better than the presidential and semi-presidential**, because in those systems one person as a rule becomes the "boss". As an example, he cites **France and Emmanuel Macron** and **America and Donald Trump** – these are people who determine a great deal with their name, surname, and character.

He admits that in Croatia, too, the **prime minister is number one of the executive branch**, but the key difference is that he must nevertheless have behind him a **majority of 76 hands**, which Orlović considers more democratic than a model in which one person decides.

sections.subtitle: Zašto Zagrepčanin ne može glasati za dobrog kandidata iz Vukovara?
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj iznosi frustraciju geografskim ograničenjem biračkog prava
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da je zakonska podjela na izborne jedinice donesena **devedesetih godina** te da Hrvatska tada nije bila jedina država koja je taj model primijenila. Priznaje da je bilo i određenih interesa, ali i pozitivnih strana – primjerice, mogućnost da se **lokalni ljudi iz određene sredine profiliraju**.

No ono što mu ostaje neshvatljivo jest činjenica da **ne može glasati za političara koji nije kandidat u njegovoj izbornoj jedinici**. "Zašto ja ne bih mogao glasati za nekoga iz Dalmacije ili iz Slavonije, Istre", pita se, umjesto da bude ograničen isključivo na zagrebački prsten u kojem živi – i to u 2026. godini.

Orlović se u potpunosti slaže i tu vidi **najveći nedostatak sustava izbornih jedinica**: birač je ograničen na mali geografski prostor i na tih četrnaest imena koja u pravilu dolaze iz tog kraja. Priznaje da iznimke postoje, osobito u jačim strankama, gdje su se pojedinci nametnuli radom, terenskim aktivnostima i govorom o problemima zajednice.

Ipak, zaključuje, bilo bi puno bolje da je **cijela Hrvatska jedna izborna jedinica**, kako bi svatko mogao birati dobrog kandidata iz **Vukovara**, iz pete ili četvrte slavonske izborne jedinice, ili nekoga iz **Dubrovnika i Splita** koji pripadaju devetoj i desetoj izbornoj jedinici.
sections.subtitle_en: Why can't a resident of Zagreb vote for a good candidate from Vukovar?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host expresses frustration with the geographical restriction of the right to vote.
sections.content_en:
The host recalls that the legal division into electoral constituencies was adopted in the **nineties** and that Croatia was not the only country back then that applied that model. He acknowledges that there were also certain interests, but also positive aspects – for example, the possibility for **local people from a specific environment to profile themselves**.

However, what remains incomprehensible to him is the fact that **he cannot vote for a politician who is not a candidate in his constituency**. "Why shouldn't I be able to vote for someone from Dalmacija or from Slavonija, Istra," he wonders, instead of being limited exclusively to the Zagreb ring where he lives – and that in the year 2026.

Orlović completely agrees and sees here **the greatest shortcoming of the electoral constituency system**: the voter is limited to a small geographical space and to those fourteen names that, as a rule, come from that area. He admits that exceptions exist, especially in stronger parties, where individuals have imposed themselves through work, field activities, and speaking about community problems.

Nevertheless, he concludes, it would be much better if **all of Croatia were one single constituency**, so that everyone could choose a good candidate from **Vukovar**, from the fifth or fourth Slavonian constituency, or someone from **Dubrovnik and Split** who belong to the ninth and tenth constituency.

sections.subtitle: Europski izbori: Hrvatska već jest jedna izborna jedinica, ali izlaznost je ispod 30 posto
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o podcijenjenoj važnosti izbora za Europski parlament i niskoj izlaznosti
sections.content:
Orlović podsjeća na paradoks: za **izbore za Europski parlament Hrvatska već jest jedna izborna jedinica** i ondje podjela na izborne jedinice ne postoji. No problem je drugi – **mizerna izlaznost, manja od 30 posto**, zbog čega rezultati nisu mjerodavni i prednost jedinstvene izborne jedinice ne dolazi do izražaja.

Smatra da se ljudi ozbiljno varaju kada te izbore doživljavaju kao nevažne. **Europska komisija i zastupnici mogu odrediti i nametnuti vrlo mnogo**, donose se zakoni koji snažno utječu na život svih građana Europske unije.

Problem vidi i u percepciji: "pijarovski su doživljeni" tako da ljudi misle da se bira **"šest-sedam nekih tamo koji će primati osam tisuća eura plaće"** – a nije baš tako. Mnogi zakoni koji se provode u Hrvatskoj, kaže, **nametnuti su izvana**, pa je upravo zato bitno tko će zastupati hrvatske građane.

Zaključak je jasan: ti su izbori podcijenjeni, i to **bez razloga**, te bi ih trebalo shvaćati puno ozbiljnije.
sections.subtitle_en: European elections: Croatia is already one constituency, but turnout is below 30 percent
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the underestimated importance of the elections for the European Parliament and the low turnout.
sections.content_en:
Orlović recalls a paradox: for **the European Parliament elections Croatia is already one constituency** and a division into constituencies does not exist there. But the problem is different – **a miserable turnout, less than 30 percent**, which is why the results are not authoritative and the advantage of a single constituency does not come to the fore.

He considers that people are seriously mistaken when they perceive these elections as unimportant. **The European Commission and representatives can determine and impose a great deal**, laws are passed that strongly affect the lives of all citizens of the European Union.

He also sees a problem in perception: "PR-wise they are perceived" in such a way that people think that **"six or seven of some people over there who will receive an eight-thousand-euro salary"** are being elected – and that is not quite so. Many laws that are implemented in Croatia, he says, **are imposed from the outside**, and that is precisely why it is important who will represent Croatian citizens.

The conclusion is clear: these elections are underestimated, and that **without reason**, and they should be taken much more seriously.

sections.subtitle: Razočaranje politikom: 'Ljudi nemaju vjeru jer su ih političari kompromitirali'
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Orlović govori o razočaranosti građana politikom i potrebi za dosljednim političarima
sections.content:
Orlović otvara i širu temu odnosa građana prema politici. U Hrvatskoj su, kaže, ljudi **nažalost i s razlogom razočarani politikom** – mnogi su ih političari razočarali i kompromitirali, pa jednostavno **nemaju vjere ni u ljude ni u politiku**.

Taj se dio, tvrdi, mora mijenjati, a promjena je moguća samo s ljudima koji su:

- **dosljedni**
- **pošteni**
- **vjerni onome što govore**
- **nepotkupljivi i "nisu na prodaju"** – u smislu političke prodaje

U tome vidi jedini put povratka povjerenja u institucije i političko djelovanje.
sections.subtitle_en: Disappointment with politics: 'People do not have faith because politicians have compromised them'
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Orlović speaks about citizens' disappointment with politics and the need for consistent politicians
sections.content_en:
Orlović also opens the broader topic of the relationship of citizens toward politics. In Croatia, he says, people are **unfortunately and with reason disappointed with politics** – many politicians have disappointed and compromised them, so they simply **have no faith either in people or in politics**.

That part, he claims, must change, and change is possible only with people who are:

- **consistent**
- **honest**
- **faithful to what they say**
- **incorruptible and "not for sale"** – in the sense of political sale

In this he sees the only path of returning trust in institutions and political action.

sections.subtitle: Matematički krimen: kako jedna stranka s 5,001 posto može pokupiti svih 14 mandata
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj razlaže hipotetski primjer izbornog praga i D'Hondtove metode
sections.content:
Voditelj otkriva da je na apsurd izbornog sustava naišao još **u šestom razredu osnovne škole, 2003. godine**, u vrijeme jednih izbora. Postavlja hipotetski, ali matematički potpuno moguć scenarij:

> Zamislimo izbornu jedinicu s **20 stranaka**. Njih **19 osvoji po 999 glasova**, a **dvadeseta stranka osvoji 1.000 glasova**. Devetnaest stranaka time ima po **4,999 posto**, a jedna **5,001 posto**. Zbog **jednog jedinog glasa** ta stranka jedina prelazi izborni prag od pet posto, ulazi u D'Hondtovu raspodjelu mandata i **pobere svih 14 od 14 mandata na četiri godine**.

Orlović to potvrđuje kao ključni problem: **neproporcionalnost glasa** – u ovom sustavu **ne vrijedi svaki glas jednako**. Upravo su takve stavke, kaže, "najveći krimeni ovakvog izbornog sustava".

Dodaje da su takvi ekstremi u teoriji mogući, a u praksi gotovo nemogući, ali da je bilo **stvarnih situacija u kojima su stranke prelazile prag i ostajale bez mandata**. Konkretno navodi vlastitu stranku: **Mostu se 2020. godine dogodilo da je u petoj izbornoj jedinici imao oko 5,5 posto, ali zbog načina računanja po D'Hondtovoj metodi nije osvojio mandat.**

Zaključak je da bi se sve takve anomalije **anulirale** kada bi Hrvatska bila jedna izborna jedinica i kada bi se prag spustio na tri posto. Voditelj sažima: problem je **kombinacija više izbornih jedinica i praga** – ukine li se samo jedan od ta dva kriterija, sve bi izgledalo drukčije.
sections.subtitle_en: Mathematical crime: how one party with 5.001 percent can pick up all 14 mandates
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host breaks down a hypothetical example of the electoral threshold and the D'Hondt method
sections.content_en:
The host reveals that he encountered the absurdity of the electoral system as early as **in the sixth grade of elementary school, in 2003**, at the time of an election. He poses a hypothetical, but mathematically completely possible scenario:

> Let us imagine an electoral constituency with **20 parties**. **19 of them win 999 votes each**, and the **twentieth party wins 1,000 votes**. Nineteen parties thus each have **4.999 percent**, and one has **5.001 percent**. Because of **one single vote**, that party is the only one to cross the five percent electoral threshold, enters the D'Hondt distribution of mandates, and **takes all 14 out of 14 mandates for four years**.

Orlović confirms this as the key problem: **disproportionality of the vote** – in this system, **not every vote is worth the same**. It is precisely such points, he says, that are "the greatest crimes of such an electoral system".

He adds that such extremes are possible in theory, and in practice almost impossible, but that there have been **real situations in which parties crossed the threshold and were left without a mandate**. Specifically, he cites his own party: **in 2020, it happened to Most that it had about 5.5 percent in the fifth electoral constituency, but due to the method of calculation according to the D'Hondt method, it did not win a mandate.**

The conclusion is that all such anomalies would be **annulled** if Croatia were one electoral constituency and if the threshold were lowered to three percent. The host summarizes: the problem is the **combination of multiple electoral constituencies and the threshold** – if only one of those two criteria is abolished, everything would look different.

sections.subtitle: Lista od 151 imena i digitalno glasovanje: tehnologija postoji, volje nema
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o mogućnosti liste od 151 kandidata i o kriptografskim tehnologijama glasovanja
sections.content:
Nastavljajući na primjer europskih izbora, voditelj postavlja logično pitanje: **zašto svaka stranka ne bi predala listu od 151 osobe za cijelu Hrvatsku?**

Tehnoloških prepreka, tvrdi, nema. Živi se u digitalnom dobu, s raznim metodama **kriptografije**, tehnologijom **blockchaina** i **asimetričnom kriptografijom**. Uz to, Hrvatska ima **osobnu iskaznicu koja je, po njegovu mišljenju, jedan od najboljih tehnoloških identifikacijskih dokumenata u svijetu**, s visokom razinom kriptografske zaštite.

Zaključak je da bi u takvom sustavu **mogućnost malverzacije bila svedena na minimum**, a transparentnost podignuta na najvišu razinu.

No tu dolazi do ključne prepreke: **da bi se nešto promijenilo u izbornom sustavu, treba doći na vlast**. Voditelj primjećuje da tijekom 36 godina hrvatske demokracije **nijedna vlast nije istaknula inicijativu za promjenu izbornog sustava** – jer kad se jednom dođe na vrh, "lijepo je ostati tamo". Pita gosta zašto je to tako i kakva je njegova percepcija, uz ogradu da nisu svi isti.
sections.subtitle_en: A list of 151 names and digital voting: technology exists, there is no will
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about the possibility of a list of 151 candidates and about cryptographic voting technologies.
sections.content_en:
Continuing on the example of the European elections, the host poses a logical question: **why wouldn't every party submit a list of 151 people for the whole of Croatia?**

There are no technological obstacles, he claims. We live in a digital age, with various methods of **cryptography**, **blockchain** technology, and **asymmetric cryptography**. In addition, Croatia has **an identity card that is, in his opinion, one of the best technological identification documents in the world**, with a high level of cryptographic protection.

The conclusion is that in such a system, **the possibility of malversation would be reduced to a minimum**, and transparency raised to the highest level.

But here comes the key obstacle: **in order for something to change in the electoral system, one needs to come to power**. The host notes that during the 36 years of Croatian democracy, **no government has put forward an initiative to change the electoral system** – because once one reaches the top, "it is nice to stay there." He asks the guest why that is so and what his perception is, with the caveat that not everyone is the same.

sections.subtitle: 'Samo bi budala mijenjala nešto što joj donosi dobre rezultate'
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava zašto velikim strankama odgovara postojeći izborni sustav
sections.content:
Orlovićev odgovor je izravan: velikim strankama – pri čemu izričito misli na **HDZ i SDP** – ovakav sustav **odgovara**. Odgovara im, kaže, jer je **krojen upravo najjačim strankama**, a takav je postavljen još devedesetih i ostao je do danas.

Rečenicu kojom zaokružuje tu misao teško je zaobići: **"Samo bi budala išla mijenjati nešto što im donosi dobre rezultate."**

Ipak, naglašava da su postojale **dvije situacije u kojima se izborni zakon mogao promijeniti**, a šanse su propuštene.

**Prva** je bila referendumska inicijativa u koju je bio uključen i **Zvonimir Troskot**, tada još ne kao političar. Cilj je bio promijeniti izborni zakon tako da se uvedu **dva ili tri preferencijalna glasa** i **prag smanji na tri posto**. Potpisi su, kaže Orlović, uspješno prikupljeni – no **Ustavni sud je proglasio velik broj potpisa nečitkima** ("ono šezdeset tisuća potpisa, karikiram"), što on naziva **krađom referenduma**, jer se strahovalo da će ljudi izaći i promijeniti izborni zakon, što vladajućim strukturama ne bi odgovaralo.
sections.subtitle_en: 'Only a fool would change something that brings them good results'
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains why the existing electoral system suits the large parties
sections.content_en:
Orlović's answer is direct: to the large parties – by which he explicitly means **HDZ and SDP** – such a system **suits them**. It suits them, he says, because it is **tailored precisely for the strongest parties**, and it was set up as such back in the nineties and has remained to this day.

The sentence with which he rounds off that thought is hard to bypass: **"Only a fool would go and change something that brings them good results."**

Nevertheless, he emphasizes that there were **two situations in which the electoral law could have been changed**, and the chances were missed.

**The first** was a referendum initiative in which **Zvonimir Troskot** was also involved, at that time not yet as a politician. The goal was to change the electoral law so that **two or three preferential votes** would be introduced and the **threshold reduced to three percent**. Signatures were, Orlović says, successfully collected – but **the Constitutional Court declared a large number of signatures illegible** ("like sixty thousand signatures, I'm exaggerating"), which he calls **the theft of the referendum**, because there was fear that people would turn out and change the electoral law, which would not suit the ruling structures.

sections.subtitle: Poziv iz 2024.: većina od 76 ruku bez HDZ-a koju Domovinski pokret nije prihvatio
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Orlović objašnjava Mostov prijedlog Domovinskom pokretu o promjeni izbornog zakona bez Vlade
sections.content:
Druga propuštena prilika, prema Orloviću, dogodila se na **posljednjim izborima 2024. godine**. Tada je, kaže, **Most prvi pozivao Domovinski pokret da ne koalira s HDZ-om**, nego da se u Saboru složi većina bez Možemo i bez HDZ-a – s jednim jedinim ciljem: **promjenom izbornog zakona**.

Gost naglašava da je to po Ustavu bilo izvedivo **bez Vlade i bez ministara**:

1. složi se **većina od 76 ruku** u Saboru
2. uputi se **zakonski prijedlog promjene izbornog zakona**
3. izglasa se **novi izborni zakon**
4. ide se na **prijevremene izbore**

Domovinski pokret na to, kaže, nažalost nije pristao. Orlović u tome vidi potvrdu vlastite teze: političari koji nisu dosljedni sami sebi, kad osjete blizinu vlasti, odjednom počnu smatrati da im postojeći sustav odgovara. Upravo je to, tvrdi, **temeljni problem hrvatske politike** – jer ljudi to razumiju, vide i na koncu se razočaraju.
sections.subtitle_en: Call from 2024: a majority of 76 hands without HDZ that Domovinski pokret did not accept
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Orlović explains Most's proposal to Domovinski pokret on changing the electoral law without the Government
sections.content_en:
The second missed opportunity, according to Orlović, occurred in the **last elections in 2024**. At that time, he says, **Most was the first to call on Domovinski pokret not to form a coalition with HDZ**, but rather to assemble a majority in the Sabor without Možemo and without HDZ – with one single goal: **changing the electoral law**.

The guest emphasizes that according to the Constitution this was feasible **without the Government and without ministers**:

1. **a majority of 76 hands** is assembled in the Sabor
2. a **legislative proposal to amend the electoral law** is submitted
3. a **new electoral law** is passed
4. they head to **early elections**

Domovinski pokret, he says, unfortunately did not agree to that. Orlović sees in this a confirmation of his own thesis: politicians who are not consistent with themselves, when they feel the proximity of power, suddenly begin to consider that the existing system suits them. Precisely that, he claims, is the **fundamental problem of Croatian politics** – because people understand it, see it, and ultimately become disappointed.

sections.subtitle: 'Most nije dvaput doveo HDZ na vlast': Zdravko Marić, Todorić i dva izlaska iz Vlade
sections.screenshot_description: Gost demantira tezu da je Most dvaput doveo HDZ na vlast i objašnjava pad obiju Vlada
sections.content:
Orlović se potom osvrće na optužbu koju Most često sluša – da je **dvaput doveo HDZ na vlast**. Tvrdi da je to **netočno**, i to u oba slučaja.

**Prva Vlada**, kaže, srušila se sama sebi jer HDZ nije mogao podnijeti koalicijskog partnera koji **ne žmiri na nečasne radnje**, koji **postavlja uvjete** i koji želi podići političko djelovanje na moralniju i pošteniju razinu.

Jednako netočnom smatra i tvrdnju da je **2016. godine Andrej Plenković izbacio Mostove ministre**. Prema Orloviću, **Mostovi ministri nisu htjeli podržati tadašnjeg ministra Zdravka Marića**, koji je bio **u sukobu interesa zbog dopisivanja s Ivicom Todorićem**, protiv kojeg se tada vodio kazneni progon.

Gost pritom ne poriče Marićeve sposobnosti: dopušta da je možda bio i solidan ministar te dobar menadžer, ali inzistira na principu – **u politici se moraju poštivati moralni standardi**, a onaj tko je u sukobu interesa trebao bi odstupiti, koliko god bio dobar.

Upravo u toj dosljednosti Orlović vidi razlog Mostova opstanka i relevantnosti sve ove godine: postoje ljudi koji prepoznaju da u politici ima onih **kojima nije najbitnije dosegnuti fotelju**. Most je, zaključuje, **dvaput bio u Vladi i dvaput pokazao da u njoj ne želi ostati pod svaku cijenu**.
sections.subtitle_en: 'Most did not bring HDZ to power twice': Zdravko Marić, Todorić, and two exits from the Government
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest denies the thesis that Most brought HDZ to power twice and explains the fall of both Governments
sections.content_en:
Orlović then reflects on the accusation that Most often hears – that it **brought HDZ to power twice**. He claims that this is **incorrect**, in both cases.

**The first Government**, he says, collapsed on its own because HDZ could not tolerate a coalition partner that **does not turn a blind eye to dishonorable acts**, that **sets conditions**, and that wants to raise political activity to a more moral and honest level.

He considers equally incorrect the claim that **in 2016 Andrej Plenković kicked out Most's ministers**. According to Orlović, **Most's ministers did not want to support the then minister Zdravko Marić**, who was **in a conflict of interest due to correspondence with Ivica Todorić**, against whom criminal prosecution was being conducted at the time.

The guest does not deny Marić's abilities in doing so: he allows that he may have been a solid minister and a good manager, but insists on the principle – **moral standards must be respected in politics**, and whoever is in a conflict of interest should step down, no matter how good they may be.

It is precisely in this consistency that Orlović sees the reason for Most's survival and relevance all these years: there are people who recognize that in politics there are those **for whom reaching an armchair is not the most important thing**. Most, he concludes, **was in Government twice and twice showed that it does not want to remain in it at any cost**.

sections.subtitle: Banke kao javna usluga: 'Nije normalno da jednim klikom odlučuju o sudbini mlade obitelji'
sections.screenshot_description: Gost kritizira bahatost komercijalnih banaka prema malom čovjeku
sections.content:
Razgovor potom skreće na ekonomiju. Voditelj podsjeća da je **Most suverenistička stranka** koja zagovara čuvanje jakih domaćih vrijednosti, a zatim otvara pitanje **banaka kao glavnog pokretača ekonomije**.

Navodi da postoje države koje su započele proces **postupne migracije bankarskog sektora u javnu uslugu**, povlačeći paralelu s odvozom smeća ili pristupom pitkoj vodi: kad bi takve usluge bile u privatnim rukama, **najsiromašniji građani postali bi robovi bez pristupa osnovnome**. Pita je li Hrvatska danas u situaciji u kojoj se zbog snažnog privatnog bankarskog sektora **iz najsiromašnijih malo po malo cijedi**.

Orlović odgovara dvaput ponovljenim **"Ja mislim da jesmo."** Banke su, kaže, postale **prebahate**, u smislu da pojedincu određuju što može, a što ne može – i to **na temelju parametara koji nisu objektivni**. Slaže se s tezom da banke **previše doprinose sudbini malog čovjeka, i to na negativan način**.

Kasnije u razgovoru tu misao produbljuje, oslanjajući se na vlastito životno iskustvo. Kao građanin, čovjek u 35. godini, oženjen i otac troje djece, kaže da mu **nije normalno da komercijalne banke jednim klikom mogu odrediti sudbinu mladog čovjeka ili mlade obitelji** – hoće li ili neće odobriti stambeni kredit, i to prema vlastitim parametrima koji objektivno nisu realni.
sections.subtitle_en: Banks as a public service: 'It is not normal that with one click they decide on the fate of a young family'
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest criticizes the arrogance of commercial banks toward the little man.
sections.content_en:
The conversation then turns to the economy. The host reminds that **Most is a sovereigntist party** that advocates preserving strong domestic values, and then opens the question of **banks as the main driver of the economy**.

He states that there are countries that have started the process of **gradual migration of the banking sector into a public service**, drawing a parallel with garbage collection or access to drinking water: if such services were in private hands, **the poorest citizens would become slaves without access to the basics**. He asks whether Croatia is today in a situation in which, due to a strong private banking sector, **the poorest are being squeezed little by little**.

Orlović replies with a twice-repeated **"I think we are."** Banks have, he says, become **too arrogant**, in the sense that they determine for an individual what they can and what they cannot do – and that **on the basis of parameters that are not objective**. He agrees with the thesis that banks **contribute too much to the fate of the ordinary man, and in a negative way**.

Later in the conversation, he deepens this thought, relying on his own life experience. As a citizen, a 35-year-old man, married and a father of three children, he says that **it is not normal to him that commercial banks can determine the fate of a young person or a young family with a single click** – whether or not they will approve a housing loan, and according to their own parameters that are objectively not realistic.

sections.subtitle: Anatomija kruženja novca: kako porezni obveznik posuđuje vlastiti novac uz kamatu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj razlaže kako fiskalni novac preko komercijalnih banaka završava kod velikih fondova
sections.content:
Voditelj razvija tezu da je **pravi novac onaj koji izdaje država**. Ako se država knjigovodstveno promatra kao firma, riječ je o **firmi koja ne može propasti**. Bankrot države, kaže navodeći **primjer Argentine**, nije ništa drugo nego **odgoda serviranja javnog duga** – ako država ne može platiti dug po svojim obveznicama (u Hrvatskoj su poznati i **trezorski zapisi**), to će se otplatiti koji mjesec kasnije, uz izgubljeno vrijeme, ali novac ljudi prije ili poslije dobivaju.

Slijedi ključno pitanje koje mu se čini suludim: ako svi moraju plaćati **fiskalni novac**, odnosno poreze koji završavaju u zajedničkoj blagajni zvanoj **državni proračun**, zar ne bi bilo logično da građani **od te iste države mogu posuditi novac uz kamatu** – tri, pet ili deset posto, svejedno – izgraditi kuću, poslovni objekt ili tvornicu, te tu kamatu vraćati natrag u sustav? Time bi se dobila **cirkularna ekonomija**.

Umjesto toga, kaže, građani novac mogu posuditi **isključivo preko komercijalnih banaka**. Poslovni subjekti mogu preko **HBOR-a**, koji ima izravnu vezu s državnim proračunom, a jedina hrvatska banka – **HPB** – po njegovu se mišljenju "baš ne ponaša patriotski" i mogla bi puno, puno bolje.

Matematiku apsurda ilustrira konkretnim izračunom: država naplati **100 eura poreza**, taj se novac posudi PBZ-u za, recimo, **102 eura**, a kad građanin dođe u banku tražiti kredit za, primjerice, **fotonaponsku elektranu**, banka mu ga posudi za **106 eura**. Razlika od četiri eura, tvrdi, završava u džepovima velikih igrača – nabraja **BlackRock, Vanguard i talijanske mirovinske fondove**. Zaključak: **građani su zapravo posudili vlastiti novac, i to uz kamatu.**
sections.subtitle_en: Anatomy of the circulation of money: how the taxpayer borrows their own money with interest
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains how fiscal money ends up with large funds through commercial banks.
sections.content_en:
The host develops the thesis that **real money is that which is issued by the state**. If the state is viewed in accounting terms as a company, it is a matter of a **company that cannot fail**. The bankruptcy of a state, he says citing the **example of Argentina**, is nothing other than a **delay in servicing public debt** – if the state cannot pay the debt on its bonds (in Croatia, **treasury bills** are also well-known), that will be repaid a few months later, with lost time, but people receive the money sooner or later.

A key question follows that seems crazy to him: if everyone must pay **fiscal money**, that is, taxes that end up in the common treasury called the **state budget**, would it not be logical that citizens **can borrow money from that same state with interest** – three, five, or ten percent, it does not matter – build a house, a business facility, or a factory, and return that interest back into the system? This would result in a **circular economy**.

Instead of that, he says, citizens can borrow money **exclusively through commercial banks**. Business entities can through **HBOR**, which has a direct link to the state budget, and the only Croatian bank – **HPB** – in his opinion "does not really behave patriotically" and could do much, much better.

He illustrates the mathematics of absurdity with a concrete calculation: the state collects **100 euros of tax**, that money is lent to PBZ for, say, **102 euros**, and when a citizen comes to the bank asking for a loan for, for example, a **photovoltaic power plant**, the bank lends it to him for **106 euros**. The difference of four euros, he claims, ends up in the pockets of big players – he lists **BlackRock, Vanguard, and Italian pension funds**. Conclusion: **citizens have actually borrowed their own money, and that with interest.**

sections.subtitle: Podravska i Splitska banka: sjećanje na vrijeme kad je Hrvatska imala svoje banke
sections.screenshot_description: Gost se prisjeća domaćih banaka i zaključuje da su za promjene potrebne poluge vlasti
sections.content:
Voditelj postavlja pitanje zašto građani već nemaju svoje banke i zar ne bi bilo logično da, primjerice, **Grad Zagreb ili Velika Gorica imaju vlastitu banku** – kakve su, podsjeća, i postojale **prije tridesetak godina**, prije nego što su prodane u privatne ruke.

Orlović na to odgovara iskreno i bez pretenzija: **nije ekonomist po struci** i lagao bi kada bi tvrdio da je duboko upućen u tu temu. No kao građanin i obiteljski čovjek ima jasan stav o bahatosti komercijalnih banaka.

Podsjeća da je Hrvatska **prije nekih dvadeset, dvadeset pet godina imala domaće banke** – navodi **Podravsku banku i Splitsku banku**. Njegov je osobni stav da bi povratak u tom smjeru bio **dobar i bolji smjer** za zemlju.

No tu dolazi do rečenice koja se provlači kroz cijeli razgovor: **za provođenje takvih politika treba doći u poziciju vlasti.** A ljudi, kaže, nažalost i dalje biraju iste. Zato zaključuje pozivom na ustrajnost:

> "Treba ostati ustrajan, treba ostati svoj, treba ostati pošten."

Vjeruje da će se ljudi s vremenom **politički preodgojiti** i shvatiti da postoje i druge opcije koje za njih same mogu napraviti puno bolje. Jer, ponavlja, **i za velike i za male stvari bitno je biti u poziciji vlasti**.
sections.subtitle_en: Podravska and Splitska banka: memory of the time when Croatia had its own banks
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recalls domestic banks and concludes that the levers of power are needed for changes.
sections.content_en:
The host asks the question why citizens do not already have their own banks and wouldn't it be logical that, for example, **the City of Zagreb or Velika Gorica have their own bank** – such as, he recalls, did exist **some thirty years ago**, before they were sold into private hands.

Orlović answers this honestly and without pretensions: **he is not an economist by profession** and would be lying if he claimed to be deeply versed in that topic. But as a citizen and family man, he has a clear stance on the arrogance of commercial banks.

He recalls that **some twenty, twenty-five years ago, Croatia had domestic banks** – he mentions **Podravska banka and Splitska banka**. His personal stance is that a return in that direction would be a **good and better direction** for the country.

But here comes the sentence that runs through the entire conversation: **to implement such policies, one needs to come into a position of power.** And people, he says, unfortunately still choose the same ones. Therefore, he concludes with a call to perseverance:

> "Treba ostati ustrajan, treba ostati svoj, treba ostati pošten."

He believes that with time people will **politically re-educate themselves** and understand that other options also exist that can do much better for them themselves. Because, he repeats, **for both big and small things, it is essential to be in a position of power**.
