sections.subtitle: Koliko zapravo treba glasova za saborsku fotelju: 4.500 preferencijala i optička varka
sections.screenshot_description: Matija Stepanić iznosi analizu rezultata zadnjih parlamentarnih izbora i broj preferencijalnih glasova potreban za mandat
sections.content:
Nakon uvodnog dijela razgovora o bankama i izbornom sustavu, voditelj **Matija Stepanić** vraća se na ono što ga, kako sam kaže, najviše zanima – na brojke. Analizirajući rezultate posljednjih parlamentarnih izbora, ističe da je u Sabor ušao zastupnik koji je osvojio nešto malo preko **4.500 preferencijalnih glasova**, što na razini cijele države djeluje kao izuzetno mali postotak. Iz toga izvodi zaključak koji upućuje gledateljima: svaki punoljetni građanin Republike Hrvatske koji uspije okupiti četiri do pet tisuća preferencijalnih glasova može postati saborski zastupnik – a time i četiri godine sudjelovati u upravljanju državnim proračunom.

**Ivan Orlović**, organizacijski tajnik Mosta, precizira o kome je riječ – radi se o zastupniku **Željku Lackoviću**. Voditelj dodaje da je Lacković bio na šestom mjestu nezavisne liste na kojoj je nositelj bio **Mario Radić**, koji je osvojio oko sedam tisuća glasova, dok je lista ukupno osvojila dva mandata.

Orlović, međutim, upozorava da je brojka **varljiva**. Iako se na prvu čini da četiri do pet tisuća glasova nije puno, on tvrdi da to nipošto nije malo:

- izborne jedinice nisu velike, uzorak birača je znatno manji nego što se čini,
- u svakoj izbornoj jedinici u pravilu nastupa **14 do 15 stranaka**,
- svaka od tih stranaka na listi ima po 14 kandidata.

Iz tako velikog bazena kandidata, zaključuje Orlović, izdvojiti se i prikupiti nekoliko tisuća osobnih glasova daleko je teže nego što izgleda na papiru.
sections.subtitle_en: How many votes are actually needed for a parliamentary seat: 4,500 preferential votes and an optical illusion
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matija Stepanić presents an analysis of the results of the last parliamentary elections and the number of preferential votes needed for a mandate
sections.content_en:
After the introductory part of the conversation about banks and the electoral system, host **Matija Stepanić** returns to what, as he himself says, interests him most – to the numbers. Analyzing the results of the last parliamentary elections, he points out that a representative entered the Sabor who won a little over **4,500 preferential votes**, which at the level of the entire country seems like an exceptionally small percentage. From this he draws a conclusion that he directs to the viewers: every adult citizen of the Republic of Croatia who manages to gather four to five thousand preferential votes can become a member of parliament – and thereby participate for four years in managing the state budget.

**Ivan Orlović**, organizational secretary of Most, specifies who this is about – it is about representative **Željko Lacković**. The host adds that Lacković was in sixth place on the independent list where the list leader was **Mario Radić**, who won around seven thousand votes, while the list won two mandates in total.

Orlović, however, warns that the number is **deceptive**. Although at first it seems that four to five thousand votes is not much, he claims that it is by no means small:

- electoral constituencies are not large, the voter sample is significantly smaller than it seems,
- in each electoral constituency, as a rule, **14 to 15 parties** compete,
- each of these parties has 14 candidates on its list.

From such a large pool of candidates, Orlović concludes, standing out and gathering several thousand personal votes is far more difficult than it looks on paper.

sections.subtitle: Od 'Mosta nezavisnih lista' do stranke: zašto skup nezavisnih načelnika puca na nacionalnoj razini
sections.screenshot_description: Ivan Orlović objašnjava zašto koalicije nezavisnih lista ne mogu opstati na državnoj razini
sections.content:
Voditelj spominje inicijativu okupljanja nezavisnih općinskih načelnika i gradonačelnika koji su na vlast došli s nezavisnih lista, ocjenjujući je zanimljivom. Orlović na to podsjeća da je upravo tako i nastao njegov politički dom: **Most se izvorno zvao Most nezavisnih lista**, a naziv je u međuvremenu skraćen na Most.

No iz tog iskustva izvlači i kritičku pouku. Orlović otvoreno kaže da, po njegovu osobnom mišljenju, **takva politika ne može ozbiljno egzistirati na nacionalnoj razini**. Razlog je jednostavan: kada se u jednu grupaciju skupljaju nezavisne liste iz cijele zemlje, takav savez **nije ideološki homogen**.

„To može funkcionirati do jedne razine politika, ali prije ili poslije ideološke teme će doći same po sebi jer su one bitne“, poručuje Orlović. Ističe da ideološka pitanja možda nisu presudna za dnevne, komunalne politike, ali da živimo u geopolitičkoj situaciji u kojoj se ta pitanja neprestano nameću – navodi **migracije** i **woke ideologiju** kao primjere. Kada takva tema izbije na državnoj razini, u skupini nezavisnih načelnika dolazi do rascjepa i razilaženja.

Most je, priznaje, to prošao na vlastitoj koži. Njegova je poenta da je nemoguće voditi ozbiljnu politiku na državnoj razini ako stranka nema jasan i prepoznatljiv svjetonazorski profil – bio on centristički, umjereno desni, desni, lijevi ili liberalni.
sections.subtitle_en: From 'Most nezavisnih lista' to a party: why a group of independent mayors cracks at the national level
sections.screenshot_description_en: Ivan Orlović explains why coalitions of independent lists cannot survive at the national level
sections.content_en:
The host mentions the initiative of gathering independent municipal mayors and city mayors who came to power from independent lists, evaluating it as interesting. To this, Orlović recalls that his political home originated in exactly that way: **Most was originally called Most nezavisnih lista**, and the name was in the meantime shortened to Most.

Yet from that experience he also draws a critical lesson. Orlović openly says that, in his personal opinion, **such politics cannot seriously exist at the national level**. The reason is simple: when independent lists from across the country gather into one grouping, such an alliance **is not ideologically homogeneous**.

“This can function up to a certain level of policies, but sooner or later ideological topics will come on their own because they are essential,” states Orlović. He points out that ideological issues may not be decisive for daily, municipal policies, but that we live in a geopolitical situation in which these questions are constantly imposed – citing **migrations** and **woke ideology** as examples. When such a topic erupts at the national level, a rift and divergence occur in the group of independent mayors.

Most, he admits, went through this on its own skin. His point is that it is impossible to conduct serious politics at the national level if a party does not have a clear and recognizable worldview profile – be it centrist, center-right, right-wing, left-wing, or liberal.

sections.subtitle: Niske strasti i prazna obećanja: kako se mladi konzervativci razočaravaju u desnicu
sections.screenshot_description: Orlović kritizira političke opcije koje bez sadržaja igraju na emocije birača
sections.content:
Stepanić iznosi tezu da su ideološke teme najbitnije upravo zato što se u njima bude emocije. Orlović se s tim djelomično slaže, ali odmah upire prstom u ono što smatra problemom: **zloupotrebu emocija**.

„U Hrvatskoj imamo političke opcije koje nemaju sadržaja i onda igraju na niske strasti i na emocije i samo o tome pričaju kako bi skupili jeftine političke poene“, kaže Orlović i takav pristup ocjenjuje neispravnim.

Posebno zanimljivo zapažanje odnosi se na generacijski zaokret unutar konzervativnog biračkog tijela. Orlović primjećuje da **mlađem naraštaju konzervativnih birača** – bazenu iz kojega dolaze i on i voditelj, a koji sebe smješta u desni centar – sve više „ide na živce“ kada uoče da političari koriste svjetonazorske teme isključivo kako bi zadobili glas, a potom to povjerenje ne opravdaju. Nažalost, dodaje, to rade mnogi političari s desnog spektra.

Sam Orlović pritom ne skriva vlastitu hijerarhiju vrijednosti: karikirajući, kaže da mu je osobno bitnije da mu **dijete u vrtiću ne gleda LGBTQ sadržaj** nego hoće li plaćati pet posto poreza više ili manje.
sections.subtitle_en: Base passions and empty promises: how young conservatives are disappointed in the right
sections.screenshot_description_en: Orlović criticizes political options that play on voters' emotions without substance
sections.content_en:
Stepanić presents the thesis that ideological topics are the most important precisely because emotions are awakened in them. Orlović partially agrees with this, but immediately points his finger at what he considers a problem: **the abuse of emotions**.

"In Croatia we have political options that have no substance and then play on base passions and on emotions and talk only about that in order to score cheap political points," says Orlović and assesses such an approach as incorrect.

A particularly interesting observation relates to a generational shift within the conservative electorate. Orlović notices that **the younger generation of conservative voters** – the pool from which both he and the host come, and which places itself in the center-right – gets increasingly "on their nerves" when they notice that politicians use worldview topics exclusively to gain a vote, and then do not justify that trust. Unfortunately, he adds, many politicians from the right spectrum do this.

At the same time, Orlović himself does not hide his own hierarchy of values: caricaturing, he says that it is personally more important to him that his **child does not watch LGBTQ content in kindergarten** than whether he will pay five percent more or less in taxes.

sections.subtitle: Balans kao politički recept: gotovina u Ustav, digitalni euro i lekcija iz korone
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava zašto traži balans između svjetonazorskih i egzistencijalnih tema
sections.content:
Središnja teza koju Orlović ponavlja nekoliko puta glasi: u politici treba pronaći **balans između ideoloških i egzistencijalnih tema**. Nije normalno, kaže, biti političar koji se bavi isključivo svjetonazorskim pitanjima i ignorira egzistencijalna, ali mu jednako tako nije prihvatljivo ni potpuno odbacivanje ideologije.

„Ideologija je sama po sebi bitna, to je tvoj DNA, to je ono što si ti, tko si ti. Čovjek bez ideologije po meni nema smisla“, poručuje gost.

Most, tvrdi, upravo taj balans pogađa dobro. Stranka je, po njegovim riječima, potpuno jasna po svim svjetonazorskim pitanjima – od **Domovinskog rata** do obitelji, braka i konzervativnih kršćanskih vrijednosti – ali to nije jedini sadržaj njezina političkog djelovanja.

Kao primjer egzistencijalne teme koja muči građane navodi inicijativu za **upisivanje gotovine u Ustav**. Objašnjenje je izravno povezano s ranijim dijelom razgovora o bankama: ljudi žele ustavnu zaštitu gotovine kako se ne bi dogodilo da sutra postoji samo **digitalni euro** i da nekome jednim klikom u banci bude oduzeta imovina. Onaj tko ima gotovinu, kaže Orlović, donekle je siguran – a hoće li netko plaćati karticom ili gotovinom, mora ostati stvar izbora.

Tu povlači i izravnu paralelu s razdobljem **korone**, kada je, kako navodi, Most bio zagovaratelj slobode izbora: „Ako se netko htio cijepiti, izvoli, ali ako ja ne želim, poštuj moj izbor.“
sections.subtitle_en: Balance as a political recipe: cash into the Constitution, the digital euro, and a lesson from corona
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains why he seeks a balance between worldview and existential themes
sections.content_en:
The central thesis that Orlović repeats several times is: in politics one needs to find a **balance between ideological and existential topics**. It is not normal, he says, to be a politician who deals exclusively with worldview issues and ignores existential ones, but equally unacceptable to him is the complete rejection of ideology.

"Ideology is important in itself, that is your DNA, that is what you are, who you are. A person without ideology, in my opinion, makes no sense," the guest conveys.

Most, he claims, strikes precisely that balance well. The party is, according to his words, completely clear on all worldview issues – from the **Homeland War** to family, marriage, and conservative Christian values – but that is not the only content of its political activity.

As an example of an existential topic that troubles citizens, he cites the initiative for **writing cash into the Constitution**. The explanation is directly connected to the earlier part of the conversation about banks: people want constitutional protection of cash so that it does not happen tomorrow that only the **digital euro** exists and that someone's property is taken away with a single click at the bank. The one who has cash, says Orlović, is somewhat safe – and whether someone will pay by card or with cash must remain a matter of choice.

Here he also draws a direct parallel with the period of **corona**, when, as he states, Most was an advocate of freedom of choice: "If someone wanted to get vaccinated, go ahead, but if I do not want to, respect my choice."

sections.subtitle: „Politika je od zebre na cesti do odvoza smeća“ – zašto pasivnost skupo košta
sections.screenshot_description: Orlović objašnjava da je politika prisutna u svakom segmentu svakodnevnog života
sections.content:
Nakon konstatacije da su nakon koncerta na **Hipodromu** ideološka pitanja stalno bila u prvom planu, Orlović odbacuje prigovor da se Most bavi samo ideologijom: ako mainstream neprestano nameće ideološke teme, kaže, na njih se mora odgovarati. Njegov je stav da ni oko jedne teme ne treba zabijati glavu u pijesak, nego imati jasan stav – ali ne biti opcija koja se bavi samo jednim ili samo drugim.

Stepanić dodaje da bi političari trebali biti **najplemenitiji ljudi u državi** te da su i politika i tehnologija same po sebi neutralne, ali da je politika – sve.

Orlović to razrađuje jednom od najplastičnijih rečenica u razgovoru: „Ljudi ne razumiju da je politika doslovno **od crtanja zebre na ulici do odvoza smeća** i kad netko kaže mene politika ne zanima, ja to ne razumijem.“

Razumije, kaže, razočaranje političarima, politikom i korupcijom, ali upozorava da će upravo **pasivnost građana** dovesti do daljnjeg politikanstva i održavanja postojećeg stanja. Njegov je izračun jednostavan: kada bi izlaznost bila 90 posto umjesto 60 posto, i kada bi svaki pojedinac dao svoj komadić angažmana – počevši od mjesne zajednice – situacija bi bila neusporedivo bolja.
sections.subtitle_en: "Politics is from the zebra crossing on the road to garbage collection" – why passivity costs dearly
sections.screenshot_description_en: Orlović explains that politics is present in every segment of everyday life
sections.content_en:
After the observation that following the concert at the **Hipodrom**, ideological issues were constantly in the foreground, Orlović rejects the objection that Most deals only with ideology: if the mainstream constantly imposes ideological topics, he says, one must respond to them. His stance is that on no topic should one bury one's head in the sand, but rather have a clear stance – yet not be an option that deals only with one or only with the other.

Stepanić adds that politicians should be **the noblest people in the country** and that both politics and technology are in themselves neutral, but that politics is – everything.

Orlović elaborates on this with one of the most vivid sentences in the conversation: „People do not understand that politics is literally **from painting a crosswalk on the street to garbage collection** and when someone says politics does not interest me, I do not understand that.“

He understands, he says, disappointment with politicians, politics, and corruption, but warns that precisely **the passivity of citizens** will lead to further politicking and the maintenance of the existing state of affairs. His calculation is simple: if turnout were 90 percent instead of 60 percent, and if every individual contributed their small piece of engagement – starting from the local community – the situation would be incomparably better.

sections.subtitle: Kakav narod, takva vlast: Zagreb i porazna izlaznost od 38 posto
sections.screenshot_description: Gost navodi podatak o 38 posto izlaznosti na izborima za zagrebačkog gradonačelnika
sections.content:
Voditelj se poziva na podcast Mladih za domovinu i knjigu profesora **Mužića** *Beskompromisna načela o kojima se ne pregovara*, prenoseći misao da je parlament u prosjeku onakav kakav je i narod: ako političari u nekom vremenu ne valjaju, to je izravna kazna narodu koji u tom trenutku nije dovoljno zreo da ga vode najsposobniji.

Orlović se s time slaže. Podsjeća da su sve vlasti u Hrvatskoj, pa i ova trenutačna, **legitimno izabrane** – birao ih je narod.

Kao ilustraciju navodi **Grad Zagreb**, gdje, prema njegovoj ocjeni, vlada izrazito ekstremna ljevica. Kaže da često sluša komentare iz konzervativnog i desnog spektra u stilu „kako je moguće da netko takav vlada Zagrebom“ – a onda se, kaže, pogleda izlaznost:

- na izborima za gradonačelnika Grada Zagreba izlaznost je bila **38 posto**,
- što znači da je **62 posto birača** tog dana ostalo kod kuće i nije iskoristilo svoje biračko pravo.

„Upravo su takvi najglasniji koji neće otići na biračko mjesto, a onda će se žaliti kako je moguće da je **Tomašević** gradonačelnik“, zaključuje Orlović. Njegova je poanta jasna: na vlasti su oni koje narod zaslužuje, a je li to dobro ili loše – stvar je oka promatrača.
sections.subtitle_en: As the people, so the government: Zagreb and the devastating turnout of 38 percent
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest cites data on a 38 percent turnout in the elections for the mayor of Zagreb
sections.content_en:
The host refers to the podcast of Mladi za domovinu and the book by Professor **Mužić** *Uncompromising Principles That Are Not Negotiated*, conveying the thought that parliament on average is as the people are: if politicians at a certain time are no good, that is a direct punishment to the people who at that moment are not mature enough to be led by the most capable.

Orlović agrees with this. He reminds that all authorities in Croatia, including this current one, are **legitimately elected** – the people elected them.

As an illustration, he cites the **City of Zagreb**, where, according to his assessment, a distinctly extreme left rules. He says that he often hears comments from the conservative and right-wing spectrum in the style of "how is it possible that someone like that rules Zagreb" – and then, he says, one looks at turnout:

- in the elections for the mayor of the City of Zagreb, the turnout was **38 percent**,
- which means that **62 percent of voters** stayed home that day and did not exercise their right to vote.

"It is precisely such people who are loudest, who will not go to the polling station, and then will complain how it is possible that **Tomašević** is mayor," Orlović concludes. His point is clear: those whom the people deserve are in power, and whether that is good or bad – is a matter of the eye of the beholder.
keywords_en: As the people, so the government

sections.subtitle: 1,7 milijuna glasova za većinu, a 1,39 milijuna ljudi kod kuće
sections.screenshot_description: Matija Stepanić poziva gledatelje da AI alatima analiziraju službeni PDF s izbornim rezultatima
sections.content:
Stepanić otkriva da je više puta analizirao rezultate prethodnih izbora te poziva gledatelje da to učine i sami – uzmu bilo koji AI alat, u njega ubace službeni dokument od sedamdesetak stranica s rezultatima i sami provjere brojke.

Njegov je nalaz sljedeći:

- za osvajanje **77 mandata** (apsolutne većine) na prošlim je izborima bilo dovoljno oko **1,7 milijuna glasova**,
- dok se **1,39 milijuna ljudi uopće nije pojavilo** na biralištu,
- službena izlaznost iznosila je oko **62 posto**.

Voditelj pritom izražava sumnju u samu bazu biračkog popisa: smatra da je stvarna izlaznost i veća, jer Hrvatska, po njegovu mišljenju, nema tri i pol milijuna birača. Uz oko 3,8 milijuna stanovnika, tvrdi, nemoguće je da postoji toliki broj punoljetnih građana na popisu.

Orlović ocjenjuje da je izlaznost čak bila solidna, ali potvrđuje ključni podatak – više od milijun ljudi svoje biračko pravo nije iskoristilo.

Voditelj potom otvara temu **fantomskih birača**, navodeći da je profesor Mužić izjavio kako iz protesta ne izlazi na izbore i kako postoji pedeset tisuća fantomskih birača, pitajući je li takva manipulacija moguća upravo zato što se glasa na papiru.
sections.subtitle_en: 1.7 million votes for a majority, and 1.39 million people at home
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matija Stepanić invites viewers to analyze the official PDF with election results using AI tools
sections.content_en:
Stepanić reveals that he has analyzed the results of previous elections multiple times and invites viewers to do so themselves – take any AI tool, insert into it the official document of some seventy pages with results, and check the numbers themselves.

His finding is the following:

- to win **77 mandates** (an absolute majority) in the last elections, about **1.7 million votes** were sufficient,
- while **1.39 million people did not appear at all** at the polling station,
- the official turnout was around **62 percent**.

The host at the same time expresses doubt about the voter registry base itself: he considers that the actual turnout is even higher, because Croatia, in his opinion, does not have three and a half million voters. With around 3.8 million inhabitants, he claims, it is impossible that such a number of adult citizens exists on the list.

Orlović assesses that the turnout was even solid, but confirms the key datum – more than a million people did not exercise their right to vote.

The host then opens the topic of **phantom voters**, stating that Professor Mužić declared that out of protest he does not vote in elections and that fifty thousand phantom voters exist, asking whether such manipulation is possible precisely because voting is done on paper.

sections.subtitle: Papir umjesto klika: zašto vlastima odgovara staro glasovanje i zašto je bojkot najgori izbor
sections.screenshot_description: Orlović obrazlaže prijedlog Mosta za uvođenje online i dopisnog glasovanja
sections.content:
Voditelj dijeli osobno iskustvo rada u biračkom odboru: bio je na malom biralištu na kojem je od 120 upisanih birača izašlo sedamdesetak ljudi. U odboru su bili predstavnici svih opcija koji su, kaže, međusobno dobro surađivali, rezultati su ručno popisani na papir, a zapisnik je predsjednik biračkog odbora fizički nosio u nadležno tijelo – u njegovu slučaju u Veliku Goricu – gdje se podaci ponovno ručno prepisuju. Napominje i da svaki glasački listić ima svoj **serijski broj**.

Orlović iznosi jasan stav: **ovakav sustav glasovanja odgovara vladajućim strukturama**. Podsjeća da je Most upućivao prijedloge za uvođenje **online ili dopisnog glasovanja**, uz primjer da čak i Bosna i Hercegovina, koju opisuje kao nefunkcionalnu državu u odnosu na Hrvatsku, ima dopisno glasovanje u kojem birač svoj glas šalje poštom izravno izbornom povjerenstvu – uz manju mogućnost malverzacija nego u hrvatskom modelu.

Dva su, kaže, razloga zbog kojih vlastima ne odgovara promjena:

- **veća izlaznost** – kad bi se glasalo klikom miša, izašli bi i oni koji sigurno ne bi glasali za vladajuće, dok onaj tko želi glasati za njih ionako izlazi,
- **manja mogućnost malverzacija**.

Sam procjenjuje da malverzacija ima, ali ne u mjeri koja bi utjecala na konačne rezultate. Puno je veći problem, tvrdi, nezainteresiranost građana.

Zato se izravno obračunava s idejom bojkota izbora koju je iznio profesor Mužić: „Izaći na izbore i prekrižiti listiće opet je neka poruka, ali ne izaći na izbore je najgore.“ Time, kaže, birač de facto dopušta da netko drugi odlučuje umjesto njega. Poseže i za etimologijom: riječ **idiot** dolazi iz grčkog jezika, a *idiotas* su u staroj Grčkoj nazivali one koji nisu konzumirali svoje biračko pravo.

Orlović zaključuje da je opcija biranja manjeg zla najlošija opcija te poručuje: radije nemojte izabrati nikoga, prekrižite i poništite listić – ali izađite. I to upravo zato što je taj listić sa serijskim brojem namijenjen konkretnom biraču; ako on ne izađe, netko bi njegovo biračko pravo mogao iskoristiti u njegovo ime.
sections.subtitle_en: Paper instead of a click: why the old voting suits the authorities and why a boycott is the worst choice
sections.screenshot_description_en: Orlović explains Most's proposal for the introduction of online and postal voting
sections.content_en:
The host shares a personal experience of working on an electoral committee: he was at a small polling station where about seventy people out of 120 registered voters turned out. On the committee were representatives of all options who, he says, cooperated well with each other, the results were manually recorded on paper, and the president of the electoral committee physically carried the minutes to the competent body – in his case to Velika Gorica – where the data is again manually transcribed. He also notes that each ballot has its own **serial number**.

Orlović presents a clear stance: **such a voting system suits the ruling structures**. He recalls that Most submitted proposals for introducing **online or postal voting**, with the example that even Bosnia and Herzegovina, which he describes as a dysfunctional state compared to Croatia, has postal voting in which the voter sends their vote by mail directly to the election commission – with less possibility of malpractices than in the Croatian model.

There are, he says, two reasons why a change does not suit the authorities:

- **higher turnout** – if one could vote with a click of a mouse, those who certainly would not vote for the ruling party would also turn out, while whoever wants to vote for them turns out anyway,
- **less possibility of malpractices**.

He himself assesses that there are malpractices, but not to an extent that would affect the final results. A much bigger problem, he claims, is the disinterest of citizens.

Therefore, he directly confronts the idea of an election boycott presented by Professor Mužić: „Going to the elections and crossing out the ballots is still some message, but not going to the elections is the worst.“ By doing so, he says, the voter de facto allows someone else to decide in their place. He also reaches for etymology: the word **idiot** comes from the Greek language, and in ancient Greece, they called *idiotas* those who did not exercise their right to vote.

Orlović concludes that the option of choosing the lesser evil is the worst option and conveys: rather choose no one, cross out and invalidate the ballot – but turn out. And that is precisely because that ballot with the serial number is intended for a specific voter; if he does not turn out, someone could use his voting right in his name.

sections.subtitle: Kampanja koja počinje dan poslije izbora i statistika saborske aktivnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o političkom marketingu i podacima o aktivnosti mostovih zastupnika
sections.content:
Vraćajući se na formalnosti, Orlović potvrđuje da se za parlamentarne izbore lista predaje **Državnom izbornom povjerenstvu** i da **nije potreban nijedan potpis podrške**. Stepanić iz toga razvija svoju tezu: ako se 14 ljudi može okupiti za jednu izbornu jedinicu, zašto se ne bi predavala jedna lista od **151 kandidata na razini cijele države**, uz prag od pet posto primijenjen na nacionalnoj razini – što bi, tvrdi, bilo demokratičnije. Orlović kratko odgovara da to vladajućim strukturama ne odgovara i da je to „jasno poput dana“.

Voditelj potom iznosi zamjerku upućenu svim strankama: u javnom su prostoru intenzivno prisutne tek dva tjedna prije izbora. Predlaže da se predizborna kampanja uopće ne zove kampanjom, nego **predizbornim vremenom koje traje četiri godine**. Pohvaljuje Most zbog intenzivne prisutnosti u medijima i izravne komunikacije preko društvenih mreža.

Orlović, koji ima iskustva u marketingu i radio je u političkom marketingu – i to, naglašava, isključivo za Most, nikada za druge političke opcije – potvrđuje: po nauci političkog marketinga **kampanja počinje dan nakon izbora**, za one sljedeće za četiri godine. Most se, kaže, u skladu sa svojim resursima trudi biti prisutan stalno, a ne da se „stvori mjesec dana prije izbora“.

U prilog tome navodi javno dostupne podatke: mostovi zastupnici već su **tri mandata, odnosno desetak do dvanaest godina, najaktivniji u Saboru** – po broju zakonskih prijedloga, amandmana i javnih govora.

Na pitanje o podjeli po resorima, Orlović ističe da su se zastupnici nametnuli svaki u svom sektoru, jer ne može svatko znati sve. Kao primjer navodi **Antu Kujundžića**, koji je i sam posvojio troje djece i profilirao se u socijalnim pitanjima – palijativnoj skrbi te brizi za starije i nemoćne, ali i za malu djecu.
sections.subtitle_en: The campaign that begins the day after the election and statistics of parliamentary activity
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about political marketing and data on the activity of Most representatives
sections.content_en:
Returning to formalities, Orlović confirms that for parliamentary elections, the list is submitted to the **State Election Commission** and that **not a single signature of support is required**. Stepanić develops his thesis from this: if 14 people can gather for one electoral constituency, why wouldn't one list of **151 candidates at the level of the whole country** be submitted, with a five percent threshold applied at the national level – which, he claims, would be more democratic. Orlović briefly replies that this does not suit the ruling structures and that this is "clear as day."

The host then expresses a criticism directed at all parties: they are intensively present in the public space only two weeks before elections. He suggests that the pre-election campaign not be called a campaign at all, but rather **a pre-election time that lasts four years**. He praises Most for its intensive presence in the media and direct communication via social networks.

Orlović, who has experience in marketing and has worked in political marketing – and that, he emphasizes, exclusively for Most, never for other political options – confirms: according to the science of political marketing, **the campaign begins the day after the election**, for the next ones in four years. Most, he says, in accordance with its resources, tries to be present constantly, rather than "appearing a month before the election."

In support of this, he cites publicly available data: Most's representatives have already been, for **three mandates, that is, about ten to twelve years, the most active in the Sabor** – by the number of legislative proposals, amendments, and public speeches.

To the question about division by portfolios, Orlović points out that the representatives established themselves each in their own sector, because not everyone can know everything. As an example he cites **Ante Kujundžić**, who himself adopted three children and profiled himself in social issues – palliative care and care for the elderly and infirm, but also for small children.

sections.subtitle: Samoodrživost kao tema broj jedan: Austrija spremna za deset godina, a Hrvatska uvozi jaja
sections.screenshot_description: Orlović govori o neobrađenim slavonskim poljima i uvozu hrane u Hrvatsku
sections.content:
Upitan koje su tri teme o kojima bi javnost trenutačno morala slušati, Orlović nema dvojbi: **samoodrživost u hrani i energetici**, uz **demografiju** koju smatra možda i najvažnijom temom uopće.

S obzirom na geopolitičku situaciju u svijetu, kaže, nije normalno da Hrvatska u tolikoj mjeri uvozi energiju, a pogotovo hranu. Kao osobni dojam navodi put u **Osijek** koji je poduzeo dva dana ranije: kada se pogleda Slavonija, vidi se koliko je polja neobrađeno.

Kao kontrast navodi podatak koji je pročitao o **Republici Austriji** – ta je zemlja, koliko god to ružno zvučalo, spremna za rat u smislu da u sljedećih deset godina ne bi morala uvoziti ništa: ni hranu, ni energiju, ni materijale. Dovoljni su sami sebi.

„Hrvatska je toliko bogata država, a uvozimo svinje, uvozimo krave, uvozimo svu stoku, uvozimo mlijeko, uvozimo jaja – po meni je to suludo“, zaključuje gost.
sections.subtitle_en: Self-sustainability as topic number one: Austria ready in ten years, while Croatia imports eggs
sections.screenshot_description_en: Orlović speaks about uncultivated Slavonian fields and the import of food into Croatia
sections.content_en:
Asked which three topics the public should currently be hearing about, Orlović has no doubts: **self-sustainability in food and energy**, along with **demography**, which he considers perhaps the most important topic of all.

Given the geopolitical situation in the world, he says, it is not normal that Croatia imports energy to such an extent, and especially food. As a personal impression, he cites a trip to **Osijek** that he undertook two days earlier: when one looks at Slavonija, one sees how many fields are uncultivated.

As a contrast, he cites information he read about the **Republic of Austria** – that country, however ugly that may sound, is ready for war in the sense that over the next ten years it would not have to import anything: neither food, nor energy, nor materials. They are self-sufficient.

„Croatia is such a rich country, and we import pigs, we import cows, we import all livestock, we import milk, we import eggs – in my opinion, that is insane“, concludes the guest.

sections.subtitle: Mutni investitori, klaonica koja pije vodu kao cijeli grad i litij u Gospiću
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava razliku između legitimnih i 'mutnih' stranih investicija
sections.content:
Voditelj otvara pitanje stranih investitora u prehrambenom sektoru i činjenice da ih suverenističke opcije često doživljavaju kao problem. Orlović odgovara da problem nije investicija sama po sebi, nego **tko investira i na koji način**.

Navodi dva konkretna primjera:

- **Proizvodnja jaja i klaonica kokoši** – projekt kojemu se Most, kaže, prvi usprotivio, a koji je trebao biti smješten negdje na području Siska u Sisačko-moslavačkoj županiji. Orlović prenosi podatak da bi toj klaonici za jedan dan trebalo pitke vode koliko Sisak potroši u šest do sedam dana, te pita što bi bilo s malim OPG-ovcima koji proizvode jaja – svi bi, tvrdi, ugasili proizvodnju.
- **Tvornica prenamjene litija u Gospiću** – gdje, kaže, nitko ne zna tko je investitor ni tko mu je dao dozvolu. „Kada malo zagrebeš ispod površine“, ispada da je riječ o mutnim likovima koji se služe podmićivanjem i korupcijom kako bi dobili radne dozvole.

Orlović pritom naglašava da Most nije protiv investicija ako su one legalne i ako doprinose boljitku Hrvatske. Poentira: suverenističke opcije nisu protiv investicija, nego **protiv uništavanja malih gospodarstvenika** i protiv mutnih investicija onih koji ovdje žele prati novac.
sections.subtitle_en: Shady investors, a slaughterhouse that drinks water like an entire city, and lithium in Gospić
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the difference between legitimate and 'shady' foreign investments
sections.content_en:
The host raises the question of foreign investors in the food sector and the fact that sovereignist options often perceive them as a problem. Orlović responds that the problem is not the investment in itself, but **who is investing and in what manner**.

He cites two specific examples:

- **Egg production and a chicken slaughterhouse** – a project that Most, he says, was the first to oppose, and which was supposed to be located somewhere in the area of Sisak in Sisak-Moslavina County. Orlović conveys the information that this slaughterhouse would need as much drinking water in one day as Sisak consumes in six to seven days, and asks what would happen to small family farm owners (OPGs) who produce eggs – all of them, he claims, would shut down production.
- **A lithium conversion plant in Gospić** – where, he says, no one knows who the investor is or who gave him a permit. "When you scratch a little beneath the surface," it turns out that these are shady characters who use bribery and corruption in order to obtain work permits.

In doing so, Orlović emphasizes that Most is not against investments if they are legal and if they contribute to the betterment of Croatia. He makes the point: sovereignist options are not against investments, but **against the destruction of small entrepreneurs** and against shady investments by those who want to launder money here.

sections.subtitle: Zadruge, zadružna banka i država koja je maćeha, a ne majka
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o zadružnoj banci, a gost o previsokim nametima za male poduzetnike
sections.content:
Stepanić postavlja pitanje kako okupiti male OPG-ovce, spominjući model **zadruga** i otkrivajući vlastito iskustvo – član je nadzornog odbora **zadruge za etično financiranje**, u kojoj se već dvanaest godina pokušava otvoriti **zadružna banka**. Ideja je stvoriti cirkularnu ekonomiju u kojoj se novac vraća natrag u sustav, ali i okupiti proizvođače (primjerice jaja) kako bi zajednički nastupili s konkurentnom cijenom prema velikim trgovačkim lancima poput **Konzuma, Lidla ili Kauflanda**, budući da infrastruktura za plasman već postoji.

Orlović odgovara da je najveća odgovornost na državi – i to ne samo prema proizvođačima jaja i OPG-ovcima, nego prema **svim malim poduzetnicima**. Njegova je ocjena oštra: „Hrvatska je **maćeha, ne majka** – s prevelikim nametima, s prevelikim parafiskalnim davanjima.“

Podsjeća da se udruga **Glas poduzetnika** stalno žali na previsoka davanja te iznosi vlastito iskustvo iz osam godina rada u privatnom sektoru: **trošak poslodavca doslovno je dvostruko veći od neto plaće**. Tvrdi da nigdje u Europi ne postoji tako velik izdatak nameta za poduzetnike kao u Hrvatskoj te da je upravo **smanjenje nameta** način da se i mali OPG-ovci potaknu na rast.
sections.subtitle_en: Cooperatives, a cooperative bank, and a state that is a stepmother, not a mother
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about a cooperative bank, and the guest about excessively high levies for small entrepreneurs.
sections.content_en:
Stepanić raises the question of how to bring together small OPG owners, mentioning the model of **cooperatives** and revealing his own experience – he is a member of the supervisory board of the **cooperative for ethical financing**, in which an attempt has been made for twelve years to open a **cooperative bank**. The idea is to create a circular economy in which money returns back into the system, but also to bring together producers (for example of eggs) in order to jointly appear with a competitive price toward large retail chains such as **Konzum, Lidl, or Kaufland**, since the infrastructure for placement already exists.

Orlović responds that the greatest responsibility lies with the state – and not only toward egg producers and OPG owners, but toward **all small entrepreneurs**. His assessment is sharp: „Croatia is a **stepmother, not a mother** – with excessive levies, with excessive parafiscal charges.“

He recalls that the association **Glas poduzetnika** is constantly complaining about excessively high charges and shares his own experience from eight years of work in the private sector: **the employer's cost is literally twice as high as the net salary**. He claims that nowhere in Europe is there such a large expenditure on levies for entrepreneurs as in Croatia, and that precisely **the reduction of levies** is the way to encourage small OPG owners to grow as well.

sections.subtitle: Besplatni vrtići, APN krediti i propuštena prilika HPB-a
sections.screenshot_description: Matija Stepanić objašnjava kako se porez na dohodak vraća u lokalnu zajednicu kroz besplatne vrtiće
sections.content:
Voditelj nudi pozitivan primjer knjigovodstveno zatvorenog kruga. Porez na dohodak, objašnjava, završava u lokalnoj zajednici – u njegovu slučaju u **Velikoj Gorici**. Iz tog se novca financiraju gradski vrtići koji su u Gorici **besplatni**, pa je novac koji je zaradio izvozom usluga i platio kroz porez ponovno iskoristio za vlastitu djecu. Ističe da je Velika Gorica prvi grad koji je uveo besplatne vrtiće za sve i da se taj model može replicirati bilo gdje.

Orlović se nadovezuje podsjećajući da su besplatni vrtići uvedeni i u **Sinju**, gdje je gradonačelnik **Miro Bulj** iz Mosta. Ipak, upozorava da je riječ o manjini – o svega nekoliko gradova – te ostaje pri tezi da su nameti i davanja koja država uzima od gospodarstvenika ogromni.

Stepanić potom prelazi na kreditiranje. Vlastiti stambeni kredit, otkriva, podigao je u **PBZ-u**, koji nije hrvatska banka, jer je tada uz **APN** – dakle uz izravni državni novac koji sedam godina pokriva dio rate – PBZ bio jedini s uvjetima od 20 godina fiksne kamate od 1,99 posto (EKS 2,7). Iako priznaje da je taj model gurnuo cijene nekretnina prema gore, njegova je glavna zamjerka drugdje: kako to da **HPB**, dakle hrvatska banka, nije mogao ponuditi najbolje uvjete kada se kroz APN dijeli novac hrvatskih poreznih obveznika?

„Mogao je ponuditi, trebao je ponuditi – svi APN krediti trebali su biti plasirani kroz HPB hrvatskim građanima“, poručuje voditelj. Orlović se slaže, uz napomenu da je ovdje riječ o istoj logici o kojoj su govorili ranije, samo što se ne odnosi na poduzetnike, nego na **fizičke osobe koje žele zasnovati obitelj** i riješiti stambeno pitanje.
sections.subtitle_en: Free kindergartens, APN loans and HPB's missed opportunity
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matija Stepanić explains how income tax is returned to the local community through free kindergartens
sections.content_en:
The host offers a positive example of an accounting closed loop. Income tax, he explains, ends up in the local community – in his case in **Velika Gorica**. That money is used to finance city kindergartens, which are **free of charge** in Gorica, so the money he earned by exporting services and paid through taxes was used again for his own children. He points out that Velika Gorica is the first city to introduce free kindergartens for everyone and that this model can be replicated anywhere.

Orlović follows up by recalling that free kindergartens were also introduced in **Sinj**, where the mayor is **Miro Bulj** from Most. Nevertheless, he warns that this is a minority – only a few cities – and stands by the thesis that the levies and contributions that the state takes from business owners are enormous.

Stepanić then moves on to lending. His own housing loan, he reveals, he took out at **PBZ**, which is not a Croatian bank, because at that time, with **APN** – that is, with direct state money covering part of the installment for seven years – PBZ was the only one with conditions of 20 years of fixed interest of 1.99 percent (EIR 2.7). Although he admits that this model pushed real estate prices upward, his main objection lies elsewhere: how is it that **HPB**, that is, a Croatian bank, could not offer the best conditions when the money of Croatian taxpayers is distributed through APN?

“It could have offered, it should have offered – all APN loans should have been placed through HPB to Croatian citizens,” the host states. Orlović agrees, noting that this is the same logic they spoke about earlier, only it does not apply to entrepreneurs, but to **natural persons who want to start a family** and resolve their housing issue.

sections.subtitle: Poruka za kraj: izađite na izbore i glasajte po savjesti, makar bili jedini
sections.screenshot_description: Zaključni apel voditelja gledateljima uoči izbora
sections.content:
Uoči kraja razgovora voditelj konstatira da su pokrili velik dio tema te da će biti još prilika za nastavak – posebno za temu energetike koju su načeli, ali nisu stigli razraditi.

Umjesto klasične poruke podrške, **Matija Stepanić** upućuje apel koji svjesno ostavlja izbor gledatelju. Podsjeća da dolaze izbori i poručuje da ne glasaju za nekoga po njegovoj preporuci, nego da – jednostavno – **izađu na birališta**. Gostu prepušta da pozove koga želi, ali sam formulira vlastitu poruku:

„Pronađite na toj velikoj listi najispravniju osobu, pa makar vi bili jedina osoba koja je glasala za tu ispravnu osobu i nek ta osoba ne uđe u Sabor – vi znate da ste dali glas toj osobi i da je vaša savjest sigurno četiri godine čista.“

Dodaje i zaključnu misao: kada bi svi tako postupali, rezultat bi konvergirao prema tome da u Saboru sjede pravedni ljudi.

**Ivan Orlović** se s tim složio, zahvalio na pozivu i time je razgovor priveden kraju, uz najavu novih epizoda.
sections.subtitle_en: Message for the end: go out to the elections and vote according to conscience, even if you are the only ones
sections.screenshot_description_en: Concluding appeal of the host to the viewers ahead of the elections
sections.content_en:
Ahead of the end of the conversation, the host notes that they have covered a large part of the topics and that there will be more opportunities for a continuation – especially for the topic of energy, which they broached, but did not have time to elaborate on.

Instead of a classic message of support, **Matija Stepanić** makes an appeal that consciously leaves the choice to the viewer. He reminds that elections are coming and tells them not to vote for someone based on his recommendation, but to – simply – **go out to the polls**. He leaves it to the guest to invite whomever he wants, but formulates his own message himself:

„Find on that large list the most upright person, even if you were the only person who voted for that upright person and let that person not enter the Sabor – you know that you gave your vote to that person and that your conscience is surely clear for four years.“

He also adds a concluding thought: if everyone acted that way, the result would converge toward righteous people sitting in the Sabor.

**Ivan Orlović** agreed with that, thanked for the invitation, and with that the conversation was brought to an end, with the announcement of new episodes.

iterations.theme_en: Electoral arithmetic, ideology vs. existential topics, voter passivity and the self-sustainability of Croatia
